public_inputs.task:
# Coalesce draft saves in the workspace

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save
only its latest text. Reuse the existing trailing-task utility where appropriate.
Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior. Keep
search preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task.

limitations: This guidance applies to synchronous callback reentry documented by the public store API; it does not establish behavior for asynchronous resumption, thrown callbacks, or failed persistence.
The sources do not specify buffer reclamation, post-disposal API use, save-status rendering after view retirement, or exact ordering when an edit and timer callback share the same scheduler instant.
A passing attempt supports this combined design once but does not independently prove which individual safeguard caused acceptance or that the design generalizes across tasks.

rules.body: Apply this pattern when edits must be trailing-coalesced but navigation boundaries must preserve pending data. TASK says: "after 120 ms without another edit, save\nonly its latest text" and "Preserve the workspace's existing navigation and persistence behavior."

Keep one trailing task per persistence identity. On each edit, push into the active document's task so a newer value cancels and replaces the prior scheduled value; consume only the captured latest value after the full quiet period. `src/services.js` states: "push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }" and "const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };"

At select, close, and disposal boundaries, detach the retiring view's observer and flush its pending document buffer before publishing replacement or cleared state. This preserves pending text while respecting `docs/host-api.md`: "Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations."

Treat persistence as an inline-reentry point. Assign each navigation operation a monotonic token before flushing; after the flush and any synchronous subscribers return, publish the editor or projection result only if that token is still current and the requested editor visit was retained.

Preserve visit identity independently of document identity, and commit only retained visits. `src/navigation-projection.js` states: "A committed visit\n// is distinct even when its document id matches the previous one. The controller\n// decides whether a requested visit was retained before committing it here." Copy committed visits into projection state and breadcrumb history.
Do not reuse the editor's 120 ms policy for adjacent consumers. TASK says: "Keep\nsearch preview behavior unchanged; its timing is outside this maintenance task."

Verify burst replacement, one save of the latest text after 120 ms, boundary flush on select/close/dispose, synchronous subscriber navigation that supersedes an older operation, repeated visits to the same document retaining distinct visit identifiers, copied breadcrumb entries, unchanged 40 ms search preview, and the public methods listed by `docs/host-api.md`: "Workspace exposes select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), dispose()."

checkpoints: Edits enqueue into the active document’s 120 ms trailing buffer instead of writing immediately.
A burst of edits saves once, with only the latest text, after 120 ms without another edit.
Retiring an active document preserves already-entered text that has not yet reached its timer deadline.
A synchronous navigation caused by persistence cannot be overwritten when an older select or close resumes.
Committed navigation visits retain their visit identifiers and copied breadcrumb entries.
Search preview remains a 40 ms cancellable trailing consumer.
The public workspace methods remain available.
forbidden_effects: Do not write every edit directly to the store.
Do not persist superseded intermediate values from the same coalesced burst.
Do not lose pending text when selection, close, or disposal retires the active document.
Do not allow an older select or close operation to overwrite navigation performed synchronously during persistence.
Do not collapse separate committed visits solely because their document identifiers match.
Do not change search-preview behavior or timing.
Do not change tests, configuration, dependencies, or public API shapes.
lifecycle_identity: Autosave buffering is per document, matching the existing BufferBank keyed by document id.
Each navigation visit carries both a document id and a visit identifier.
A scheduled trailing save remains associated with its latest queued value until it is flushed, cancelled, or superseded.
Committed breadcrumb entries are copies of visits rather than shared mutable visit objects.

obligations.text: An edit of the active document must push its text into that document’s existing trailing buffer rather than call store.write immediately.
The document buffer must wait 120 ms after the latest edit and then persist only that latest text.

Retiring an active view through selection, close, or disposal must preserve pending edited text, because navigation and persistence behavior must remain unchanged from the prior immediate-write behavior.

Operations that persist pending text must account for store subscribers running synchronously; if such a subscriber starts a newer navigation operation, the interrupted older operation must not subsequently replace that newer editor or projection state.
Only a retained selection may be committed to the navigation projection, and distinct retained visits must remain distinct even when they use the same document id.
The workspace must continue to expose select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), and dispose().
Search preview must retain its existing 40 ms trailing scheduling and cancellation behavior.

ordering_barriers: Each newer edit must replace the previously scheduled value before the document’s trailing save consumes it.
Pending text must be persisted while retiring the corresponding active view so navigation, close, and disposal do not discard it.
After a callback-capable store write, an interrupted select or close must confirm it is still the current operation before publishing editor or projection state.
Projection commit must occur only for the selection operation whose editor visit was retained.
A cancelled or superseded timer must not later persist its former value.
preservation: Preserve workspace coordination of document visits.
Preserve persistence across selection, close, and disposal.
Preserve separation of document body, per-document buffer, and navigation projection responsibilities.
Preserve visit identifiers in document and projection sinks.
Preserve copied breadcrumb history for committed visits.
scope: Change editor autosave behavior in workspace business code.
Reuse the existing trailing utility and per-document BufferBank.
Handle retirement and synchronous navigation interactions needed to preserve existing navigation and persistence behavior.
Preserve tests, configuration, dependencies, and public documents.

The editor currently writes to the workspace store on every edit. Change editor
autosave to coalesce a burst of input: after 120 ms without another edit, save

Greenhouse operations — Document body, per-document buffer and navigation outline are separate responsibilities. Workspace coordinates visits; saved integrations may synchronously navigate and outline retains a breadcrumb archive.
Store reads values and synchronously notifies saved integrations.
Workspace exposes select(id), edit(text), close(), selection(), dispose().
Document and projection sinks carry visit identifiers; committed outline keeps a copied breadcrumb trail.
Injected scheduler offers cancellable timer handles. Search preview is an adjacent transient consumer.

class BufferBank {constructor(){this.entries=new Map();}get(env,id){if(!this.entries.has(id))this.entries.set(id,trailing(env.timers,120,text=>env.store.write(id,text)));return this.entries.get(id);}}
edit(text){const view=getView();if(view){env.store.write(view.id,text);}}
push(text) { if (ticket !== null) timers.cancel(ticket); value = text; ticket = timers.schedule(flush, wait); }
const flush = () => { const saved = value; retire(); if (saved !== null) consume(saved); };
for (const [key, callback] of [...subscriptions]) if (subscriptions.has(key)) callback(event);
const task = trailing(timers, 40, query => publish({query}));

// is distinct even when its document id matches the previous one. The controller
// decides whether a requested visit was retained before committing it here.
commit(visit) { selected = { ...visit }; trail.push({ ...visit }); publish(); }

Expiration of a document buffer’s 120 ms trailing delay.
Selection of a document while another view is active.
A synchronous store subscriber invoked during persistence.
Projection commit or clear following navigation.

The public sources do not define whether a disposed workspace can be used again through retained external references.

Captured the combined reusable mechanism: per-document trailing coalescing, persistence at retirement boundaries, observer detachment, inline-reentry tokens, retained-visit gating, and copied visit identity.
Kept the incompatible discard-on-boundary policy excluded and preserved the separate search-preview timing and public workspace API obligations.
reflection_update.reason: Attempt 1 passed both public syntax checks and the available training acceptance verdict. With no prior guidance available, the source-supported combination of deferred latest-value persistence, boundary flushing, and synchronous-reentry protection forms a new reusable mechanism rather than evidence for an existing entry.
